questions.orientation: Before revealing practice feedback, decode the separate count-format example and predict its malformed-file behavior. Record your confidence as uncertainty, not a grade.
questions.hypotheses: State two competing explanations of the reservation log and predict a result that would distinguish them. Save before executing the probe.
questions.probes: For every chosen raw file give bytes, predicted output, reason it distinguishes hypotheses, actual output and what remains uncertain. Describe malformed versus rejected operations.
questions.model: Give field offsets/widths and bounds; explain the state transitions; attach first decoder/model and instruction evidence for decode_record, apply_record and replay. Save before checking.
questions.repair: Retain the exact counterexample and earlier code. Explain the false assumption, minimal repair and regression probe. If no failure occurred, record a deliberately challenged alternative and its counterexample without claiming a repair.
questions.transfer: Before running reserve-atomic, predict final versus event states for a log with accepted, rejected and later accepted entries. Revise the transaction-boundary hypothesis with native and call evidence; compare reserve-opt without source-shape assumptions.
questions.handoff: Commit a genuinely fresh prediction before executing it, then retain the comparison as a new record. Export and resume the investigation with exact manifest, raw probes, commands, model, evidence, assistance and limitations so another person can reproduce it.
